NOTE: the run members, and what a shared shape costs a mutation set
why: The four detectors are one function written four times -- the object emitted all four in full with no call between them -- so a mutation in one of them is a mutation the other three do not have.  That is why the local names differ between them: an anchor that matched two of the four would be reported UNUSABLE, and UNUSABLE does not fail a run (finding F1264).  What the entries below cover is every constant the four disagree on (6 against 12, 0x38/0x07 against 0xccc/0x333, +0x04 against +0x08/+0x0c/+0x10), the sign test that puts a ZERO sample on the negative side, the equality against the limit, and reset's rounding.  Nothing here can mutate the ORDER of the two stores in a group's tail, because the counter and the register are cleared on every path and no observer sees them between.
